        city:
          title: City

          title: Telephone number
          description: >-

              title: Customer code
              description: >-

## Summary

The spec required that owner responses carry a `bulkSignupWarning` flag — `true` once **more than 80** owners have already been registered for the current business day, otherwise `false`. The acceptance test reads it back via `GET /api/owners/{id}` and asserts `false` on a fresh create.

Following the codebase's established pattern (derived owner fields are declared as `readOnly` properties in the OpenAPI schema and surfaced on the generated `OwnerDto`), I made two changes:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Added a `bulkSignupWarning` readOnly boolean property to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` gains the field.

2. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`**
   - Added a `BULK_SIGNUP_WARNING_THRESHOLD = 80` constant.
   - Extracted the daily-count logic into a shared `countOwnersRegisteredOn(LocalDate)` helper (the daily-limit rule now reuses it), since the warning accumulates over the same per-business-day bucket — exactly what the test comment describes.
   - Added `applyBulkSignupWarning(OwnerDto)`, which sets the flag to `count > 80` for the current business day (`toBusinessDay(LocalDate.now())`, consistent with how new registrations are dated).
   - Called it on both the `getOwner` and `addOwner` response DTOs.

Unmapped-target handling: MapStruct isn't configured to error on unmapped targets, so adding the field (which has no source on the `Owner` entity) is safe — the controller populates it explicitly.

`Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` and `BUILD SUCCESS`.
